statement: On a square grid, the point P is at (3, 7). P is reflected in the horizontal line y = 4, and then the new point is reflected in the vertical line x = 5. Where does P end up?

choices.misconception: I did the first reflection, to (3, 1), and forgot the second one.
I skipped the reflection in y = 4 and only reflected (3, 7) in the line x = 5.
I moved the point onto each line instead of across it, first to (3, 4) and then to (5, 4).
I did the first reflection correctly, then moved the point 2 units, its distance from x = 5, but away from the line instead of across it.

hints: Do one reflection at a time.
A reflection in a horizontal line keeps x the same and puts the point the same distance away on the other side of the line. A reflection in a vertical line keeps y the same.
P is 3 units above y = 4, so its image is 3 units below, at (3, 1). Now (3, 1) is 2 units to the left of x = 5.

solutions.reliable: P = (3, 7) is 3 units above the line y = 4, so its reflection is 3 units below the line: (3, 1). That point is 2 units to the left of the line x = 5, so its reflection is 2 units to the right of it: (7, 1). The transferable idea: a reflection keeps the coordinate that runs along the mirror line and sends the point the same distance to the other side.
solutions.elegant: Reflecting in y = 4 sends y to 8 - y, and reflecting in x = 5 sends x to 10 - x. So (3, 7) goes to (10 - 3, 8 - 7) = (7, 1). In fact, two reflections in perpendicular lines make a half turn about the point where the lines cross, here (5, 4).

whyOnTest: Reflection questions test whether you jump across the mirror line by the same distance, one step at a time, rather than sliding onto it.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
